ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, a watch with its dial facing upward can be seen; the upper side of the dial corresponds to north, the right side corresponds to east, and the left side corresponds to west. The longer minute hand points to the upper right, that is, the northeast direction; the target direction is the upper left, that is, the northwest direction. The minute hand moves clockwise, so it cannot turn directly counterclockwise from northeast to northwest, but must go clockwise through east, south, west, and then to northwest. This turning angle is 270 degrees. The minute hand turns 6 degrees per minute, so the required time is 270 ÷ 6 = 45 minutes.

method.method_draft: Use angular motion of the minute hand. Read that the watch face is upward and the minute hand initially points north-east; the image can be used to confirm the hand is around the 1:30/NE direction. The target is the first time the minute hand points north-west. Since a minute hand moves clockwise, it cannot take the shorter 90-degree counterclockwise turn from NE to NW; it must travel clockwise through east, south, and west, covering 270 degrees. At 6 degrees per minute, the time is 270 ÷ 6 = 45 minutes.
